title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and tingling in feet.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old individual presenting for a routine follow-up regarding their type 2 diabetes mellitus. They report ongoing sensations of tingling and numbness in the lower extremities. The patient has been on long-term insulin therapy for several years and does not take any oral medications for their condition. They report that the symptoms in their feet have been persistent but stable over the last three months.

Medication List
Insulin.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination of the lower extremities reveals diminished sensation to light touch in the toes. Motor strength is intact. No visible ulcers or skin breakdown noted.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on insulin.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient presents with symptoms of peripheral neuropathy. It is noted that this condition is not related to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Monitor blood glucose levels regularly. Schedule a follow-up appointment in three months to monitor the progression of the neuropathy.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
